note: The single declared 3-process supervision / crash-recovery contract (tempdoc 627). For each supervised process and fault mode: the declared detection -> recovery -> terminal-state, plus guard(s) — a test that exercises the row, or an explicit sentinel where a unit test is infeasible (real OOM, Windows-only exit codes, process-suspend hangs). This is the 'single authority rather than scattered monitor/spawner logic' the tempdoc's Goal 2 asks for, covering BOTH the Worker (Body) and llama-server (Brain), including external-adoption. Asserted by SupervisionContractTest: (1) the per-process `policy` block must equal the live policy record defaults (SupervisionPolicy / BrainSupervisionPolicy) — drift fails the build; (2) every fault mode is present per process; (3) every guard resolves to a real test file or an allowed sentinel. Lane F stage A item A11 retired the Worker entry (`status: "retired"`): the Worker is no longer a process, and the Engine's own supervisor contract lands at stage B (design 7.1). A retired entry is skipped by assertions (1) and (3) and still checked by (2). It is skipped by (3) on purpose: the guards a retired row names were deleted with the thing they guarded, so resolving them would fail the build for the retirement itself — see the Worker entry's `guardsNote` for which of its FQCNs no longer exist.

policy.note: HISTORICAL as of A11: these were SupervisionPolicy.DEFAULT_* when the Worker was a process. Nothing asserts them against code any more because the record is deleted. Stage B declares the Engine supervisor's own numbers.

faultModes.recovery: respawn (no graceful stop — process already gone), shared restart budget

faultModes.detection: (historical, A11) gRPC health-failure streak (KnowledgeServerBootstrap.checkHealth -> WorkerSpawner.recordHealthResult, 10s poll, threshold 3) while the process is alive
faultModes.recovery: graceful signal-bus stop then respawn, shared restart budget

faultModes.detection: (historical, A11) 1s death monitor (OOM exits the JVM non-zero -> seen as process death; -XX:+HeapDumpOnOutOfMemoryError dumps)
faultModes.recovery: respawn (OOM is not distinguished from clean death by the decision)
faultModes.terminalState: capability DEGRADED + worker.restart_exhausted after cap (recurring OOM trips the cap)
faultModes.note: Decision treats OOM as clean death (exit code not inspected); SupervisionDecisionTest pins that mapping. A real OOM-loop -> give-up is a dev-stack smoke.

faultModes.detection: (historical, A11) worker-side heartbeat suicide-pact (MmfWorkerSignalBus.shouldDie, 5s stale, 15s grace) corroborated by Head-PID liveness (WorkerLivenessDecision, tempdoc 630) + Windows Job Object KILL_ON_JOB_CLOSE
faultModes.recovery: worker self-exits when the heartbeat is stale AND Head's PID is dead (or no PID signal — standalone/legacy); OS force-kills on Head crash (Windows). Heartbeat-only on Linux/macOS where the Job Object is absent.
faultModes.terminalState: worker process exits (no orphan outliving a dead Head)
faultModes.livenessContinuity: (historical, A10/A11) tempdoc 630: a stale heartbeat is only actionable if Head was continuously live during the measurement window. A stale beat ALONE no longer kills — it must be corroborated by Head-PID death (WorkerLivenessDecision.HeadLiveness != ALIVE), because an OS suspend/resume produces a benign stale beat while Head (its PID persisting across suspend) is alive. UNKNOWN (no PID forwarded — standalone/tests) preserves the pre-630 heartbeat-only behavior. Guard: WorkerLivenessDecisionTest.
faultModes.note: Real-process coverage is opt-in systemTest (ChaosSuiteTest.workerDiesWhenHeartbeatStale) + WindowsJobObjectTest.assign_killsChildOnClose. The suspend/resume false-suicide is guarded fast in-process by WorkerLivenessDecisionTest (stale beat + Head ALIVE => no suicide).

faultModes.detection: (historical, A11) awaitPort timeout (spawned but never published gRPC port), or PID validation exhausting its window (PidValidationTimeoutException) — the confirmed 821 §O.4 signature
faultModes.recovery: initial boot: KnowledgeServerBootstrap.startWithRetry re-attempts transient failures (3 attempts, supervision-vetoed). If those are exhausted the bootstrap is NO LONGER discarded (tempdoc 825): KnowledgeServerHealthMonitor is constructed regardless of outcome and takes its boot-recovery arm — a bounded, backed-off re-attempt sequence under BootRecoveryPolicy (4 attempts, 10s doubling to 60s) decided by the pure BootRecoveryDecision, holding the capability at RECOVERING for the arc so a boot that ultimately succeeds narrates no flap. On success the monitor performs the HeadAssembly/LocalApiServer handover. Restart path: doRestart reaps the port-less orphan (stopProcess graceful); next supervision tick restarts or gives up from a clean slate.
faultModes.terminalState: capability DEGRADED + worker.spawn_recovery_exhausted once the boot-recovery budget is spent (distinct from supervision's worker.restart_exhausted, which boot recovery may never supersede — see recoveryAuthorityBoundary); no port-less zombie holding the data-dir lock
faultModes.recoveryAuthorityBoundary: Tempdoc 825 §D5 decision 2: BootRecoveryDecision governs ONLY the never-started state and stands down — without narrating — when supervision engaged during the failing attempt (KnowledgeServerBootstrap.supervisionEngagedOnLastAttempt) or already declared worker.restart_exhausted. So the two authorities never both hold the restart budget, and supervision's terminal verdict stays terminal.
faultModes.note: BootRecoveryDecisionTest pins the decision law (budget, backoff, both vetoes, narrate-once); KnowledgeServerBootRecoveryTest drives a real bootstrap against an empty temp dir through the monitor's arm. The orphan reap lives in WorkerSpawner.doRestart's failure path; exercising THAT needs a real spawn that never publishes a port — still a dev-stack smoke.

processes.guardsNote: HISTORICAL as of A11, and deliberately not resolvable. Three of the guard FQCNs below name test classes deleted with the code they pinned: `io.justsearch.app.services.worker.SupervisionDecisionTest` (clean-exit, hang, oom) and `io.justsearch.app.util.WindowsJobObjectTest` (zombie) went at A11; `io.justsearch.indexerworker.loop.WorkerLivenessDecisionTest` (zombie) went at A10 with WorkerLivenessDecision itself, whose only production consumer was MmfWorkerSignalBus.shouldDie — the suicide pact has no reader inside one JVM. They are kept verbatim so the row still records what USED to guard each fault mode; SupervisionContractTest.everyGuardResolves skips a retired entry, which is what stops them failing the build. The ones that DO still resolve are `io.justsearch.systemtests.ChaosSuiteTest` (zombie) and `io.justsearch.app.services.worker.{BootRecoveryDecisionTest,KnowledgeServerBootRecoveryTest}` (partial-boot) — the latter pair because A11 kept the boot-recovery arm. Stage B's replacement entry must name guards that resolve, since it will not be retired.
processes.retiredNote: retired at lane F stage A: the Worker is no longer a process; the Engine's supervisor contract lands at stage B (design 7.1). The row is kept rather than deleted so the register still records what the split gave and what stage A deliberately gave up (stage A §10: no crash detection, no restart budget, no cooldown, no stability window; a crashed Engine stays down until the user restarts it). Its `authority` (SupervisionPolicy) and `decisionSeam` (SupervisionDecision) were deleted with WorkerSpawner at A11, so SupervisionContractTest skips the live-policy equality check for a retired entry — the Brain's check is unaffected and still runs. When stage B gives the Engine a supervisor, this entry is replaced (not un-retired): the supervised thing is a different thing.

faultModes.recovery: restart with backoff (0ms first crash, crashRecoveryDelayMs after), reset on healthy restart
faultModes.terminalState: forceOffline -> Mode.OFFLINE + bounded failure-history after maxCrashes; capability OFFLINE via InferenceCapabilityWiring

faultModes.detection: periodic /health poll (LlamaServerOps.schedulePeriodicHealthCheck, periodicHealthIntervalMs, consecutiveFailuresBeforeRestart) while the process is alive
faultModes.recovery: managed: handleServerCrash (restart). external-adopted: goOfflineFromExternalFailure (no restart — no handle).

faultModes.detection: Process.waitFor crash monitor (OOM exits the server process -> same path as clean-exit crash)
faultModes.note: OOM is a process crash; LlamaServerOps.handleServerCrash handles it identically to clean-exit (exit code not distinguished). Covered by the clean-exit guard; a real GPU-OOM loop is a dev-stack smoke.

faultModes.detection: LlamaServerOps.waitForServerHealth: process exits during model load, or /health never ready before healthCheckTimeoutMs deadline (diagnosed via log-tail: arch mismatch / CUDA OOM / missing DLL / port-in-use)
faultModes.recovery: throw ModeTransitionException -> revert to prior mode (OFFLINE), failure diagnosed and recorded
faultModes.terminalState: OFFLINE with a typed startup-failure reason
faultModes.note: waitForServerHealth diagnosis path; a real partial boot (bad model / missing DLL / 120s timeout) is a dev-stack smoke — too slow/platform-specific for a unit test.

faultModes.detection: adoptExistingServerIfPresent on every start (health + /props probe, policy gates)
faultModes.recovery: adopt an externally-started server instead of spawning (no restart loop); health-only adoption behind a dev sysprop; admin policy can forbid external; an adopted server that fails health -> forced OFFLINE (cannot restart — no process handle)
faultModes.terminalState: OFFLINE on adopted-server failure (recovery deliberately declined — by design)
